exhibits.description: Unverified statements from five staff members
observations: Nora: 'I only visited the east corridor and left.'
Eli: 'I did not approach the lab after 18:00.'
Maya: 'I carried a cardboard supply box at 18:11.'
Theo: 'I remained in the cafeteria from 18:12.'
Ada: 'I staffed reception.'
exhibits.interpretation: Nora's statement describes route taken but does not explicitly deny taking prototype; V04 shows teal-coated person with prototype at East Exit which contradicts implication of innocent passage. Other statements consistent with visual evidence.

observations: 17:00 Eli: 'My project needs that prototype tomorrow.'
17:10 Maya: Request to move cardboard consumables box to loading bay
17:20 Security: 'Coat descriptions are from shift assignments; doors log badge credentials, not biometric identity. Service corridor is a camera blind spot.'
exhibits.interpretation: Security message clarifies identification limitations (badges not biometric, coats are shift assignments); Eli's message establishes potential motive but not involvement
exhibits.limitations: Messages do not prove actions taken during incident window; coat color mapping comes from case brief, not D03

key_findings.finding: Teal-coated person possessed prototype at East Exit at 18:14
Nora Vale's badge credential used for corridor entry and exit

contradictions.issue: Nora's statement vs V04 visual evidence
contradictions.description: Nora states she 'only visited the east corridor and left' but V04 shows teal-coated person with prototype at East Exit. Statement does not explicitly deny taking prototype.
contradictions.resolution: Visual evidence of possession contradicts implication of innocent passage

contradictions.description: D01 records Nora Vale's badge use, but D03 clarifies badges are not biometric identifiers
contradictions.resolution: Cannot definitively identify person as Nora Vale based on badge alone

limitations_summary: No camera captured the actual theft moment
Badge credentials do not equal biometric identification (D03)
Coat colors are shift assignments, not unique identifiers (case brief/D03)
Service Corridor blind spot creates unobserved movement possibility (V10, D03)
Single timestamp snapshots do not provide continuous alibis
No authorization records reviewed to confirm or deny legitimate removal
